title: PwnEscape's 9.3 CVSS KVM Flaw Gives VM Guests Root Host Control
summary:
Security researchers have released the technical specifications for a vulnerability that allows code running in a virtual machine to take over the physical server it resides on. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-99999, affects multiple industry-standard hypervisors using the Linux kernel networking stack and carries a critical CVSS score of 9.3. Attackers exploiting the bug can move from untrusted VM code to perform host-kernel memory reads, controlled writes, and root command execution.

The vulnerability, named PwnEscape, was published on October 15. A separate researcher, 0x4d31, noted that they were able to rediscover the flaw in under 2 hours by using OpenAI's gpt-5.6-cyber model in a devbox. The rediscovery was triggered after the researcher identified the word "virtio" in a partially redacted Vercel bounty screenshot and provided that hint to the AI agent.

now that the KVM escape details are out (https://t.co/5QFoYyonbX)… if you’re wondering how i managed to rediscover it in under 2 hours after seeing the vercel bounty screenshot:

i gave openai’s gpt-5.6-cyber (daybreak red) access to a devbox to experiment and explore different directions for 1.5 hours.

then i spotted that the word after “guest-controlled” in the screenshot wasn’t properly redacted. those 3 dots gave away “virtio”. might seem like a small hint, but i passed it to my agent, and it got excited and found the vulnerability in 30 minutes. :))

opsec lesson right there.
